items.actClause:
AN ACT in relation to a study of the number of children in foster care who
have a developmental disability
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8679

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act in relation to a study of the number of children in foster care
who have a developmental disability

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to study the placement in foster care of
children who have a developmental disability.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would require the Commissioner of the Office of
Children and Family Services (OCFS), in consultation with the Commis-
sioner of the Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD,)
to conduct a study to determine the number of children who have been
placed in foster care and who have been diagnosed with a developmental
disability. The study shall include an assessment of the demographics of
such children, and evaluation of the current guidelines and regulations
used to oversee the placement and treatment of such children, and an
analysis of the extent to which such age-appropriate children are
prepared for a transition from foster care to an independent living
situation.

Section 2 of this bill would define the term "developmental disability."

Section 3 of this bill would authorize the Commissioner of OCFS and the
Commissioner of OPWDD to acquire directly from the head of any depart-
ment, agency, or instrumentality of the State, available information
which the departments consider useful in the discharge of their duties,
and requires all departments, agencies, and instrumentalities of the
State to furnish all information requested by the departments to the
extent permitted by law.

Section 4 of this bill would require the Commissioner of OCFS and the
Commissioner of OPWDD to submit a report of the findings of the study to
the Governor and legislative leaders of the Senate and Assembly no later
than one year following the effective date of this act. The report shall
also include recommendations on how to consistently maintain a record of
the number of children who have been placed in foster care who have been
diagnosed with a developmental disability, recommendations to improve
the placement and treatment of children in foster care. and recommenda-
tions to further develop existing guidelines and regulations to prepare
age-appropriate children who have a developmental disability for a tran-
sition to an independent living situation.

Section 5 of this bill provides that the effective date shall take
effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Nationally, anywhere from 30's to 5n of the youth involved in child
protective services have some type of disability (e.g., intellectual and
Developmental Disability MD), emotional, behavioral).  Unfortunately, in
New York State there is currently no mechanism to identify which chil-
dren and youth involved with the child welfare system are diagnosed with
a disability. Understanding the breadth and depth of the problem of
persons with IDD in foster care is critical for several reasons.

First, individuals with IDD are more likely than their counterparts to
remain in foster care placements until they age out as adults.  There-
fore, it is critical for effective future planning for the youth and for
the service systems in the State to have an accurate understanding of
the number of individuals who will need connections to services and
service systems, including residential placement options.

Second, these children and youth with IDD may be placed in voluntary
placement as the only means for families to obtain needed supports for
their children; thus, these children are more likely to be in need of
continued services that specifically meet their unique needs.  This
group of youth are more likely to experience trauma, disruptions, live
in congregate care, and age out of the foster care system. Additionally,
individuals with IDD are highly susceptible to abuse. This includes
sexual abuse and particularly transactional sexual abuse with individ-
uals with IDD transitioning from child welfare setting.

Third, data collected between 2014 and 2016 through a grant funded by
the New York Developmental Disabilities Planning Council (DDPC) demon-
strated that individuals with IDD in New York are often unprepared for
transition out of foster care, have few if any community contacts in
their home communities, and lack access to needed mental health treat-
ment. These are all issues that will interfere with successful transi-
tion out of foster care and ensuring these individuals, who are already
at a significant disadvantage, will achieve any meaningful quality of
life.

Planning for transition to adulthood in New York schools for individuals
with IEPs starts at age 14. The process can be significantly enhanced if
there is clear identification of the youth that are in foster care with
IDD and the need for multiple systems to be at the table. This bill
would study the placement in foster care of children who have a develop-
mental disability.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2023-24: S.31119 (Mannion) - Veto Message 42.

2021-22: S.8046-A (Mannion) - Veto Message 59.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 89 Chapter 663
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 8679-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the social services law, in relation to requiring
        maintained records for certain children to include whether  they
        have  a  developmental disability; and conducting a study on the
        number of children in foster care who have a developmental disa-
        bility"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require the commissioner of the Office of Children and
Family Services (OCFS) to maintain information about whether a child  in
foster  care  has  an intellectual or developmental disability. It would
also require OCFS, in consultation  with  the  Office  for  People  With
Developmental  Disabilities  (OPWDD),  to  conduct  a  study on youth in
foster care who have been diagnosed with a developmental disability.
 
  Children with intellectual and developmental disabilities deserve  the
best  possible care and treatment. This population is overrepresented in
foster care, and I am  supportive  of  a  requirement  to  improve  data
collection so that the needs of these children can be better understood.
However, changes are necessary to retain the data collection requirement
but  take  out  the  requirement  for a study, which would have posed an
expense that is not accounted for in the State's financial plan.
 
  I am pleased to have reached an agreement with the Legislature to make
these changes. On the basis of this agreement, I am pleased to sign this
bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Requires that every court, and every public board, commission, institution, or officer having powers or charged with duties in relation to abandoned, delinquent, destitute, neglected or dependent children who shall receive, accept or commit any child shall provide and keep a record showing if such child has a developmental disability; requires a study of the number of children in foster care who have a developmental disability.
title: Requires maintained records for certain children to include whether they have a developmental disability; requires a study of the number of children in foster care who have a developmental disability
